response.rationale: Childhood nyctalopia, flat rod ERG, inferonasal scotoma, hyperfluorescent ring, and peripheral photoreceptor/RPE loss best fit a rod-cone degeneration/RP, compatible with nonpigmentary RP. Choroideremia is the closest alternative but less consistent with the yellow-spot nonpigmentary fundus and perifoveal inner-retinal thickening.

rejected.why: Choroideremia would more commonly show diffuse choroidal/RPE atrophy; it does not explain the yellow-spot fundus, hyperfluorescent ring, and perifoveal inner-retinal thickening pattern.
Nonspecific choroidal dystrophy does not account for the flat rod ERG, inferonasal scotoma, hyperfluorescent ring, and eccentric photoreceptor/RPE loss.
Cone-rod dystrophy is unlikely because color vision and central acuity are preserved, and the flat rod ERG indicates rod-predominant degeneration.
